--src: Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.PadicNumbers
theorem rat_dense (q : ℚ_[p]) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ r : ℚ, ‖q - r‖ < ε :=
  let ⟨ε', hε'l, hε'r⟩ := exists_rat_btwn hε
  let ⟨r, hr⟩ := rat_dense' q (ε := ε') (by simpa using hε'l)
  ⟨r, lt_trans (by simpa [Norm.norm] using hr) hε'r⟩

  simp only [mahlerTerm, ContinuousMap.smul_apply', ContinuousMap.const_apply]

--src: Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.Hensel
theorem padic_polynomial_dist {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (F : Polynomial ℤ_[p]) (x y : ℤ_[p]) :
    ‖F.eval x - F.eval y‖ ≤ ‖x - y‖ :=
  let ⟨z, hz⟩ := F.evalSubFactor x y
  calc
    ‖F.eval x - F.eval y‖ = ‖z‖ * ‖x - y‖ := by simp [hz]
    _ ≤ 1 * ‖x - y‖ := by gcongr; apply PadicInt.norm_le_one
    _ = ‖x - y‖ := by simp

--src: Mathlib.NumberTheory.Padics.PadicNumbers
theorem exi_rat_seq_conv {ε : ℚ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N, ∀ i ≥ N, padicNormE (f i - (limSeq f i : ℚ_[p]) : ℚ_[p]) < ε := by
  refine (exists_nat_gt (1 / ε)).imp fun N hN i hi ↦ ?_
  have h := Classical.choose_spec (rat_dense' (f i) (div_nat_pos i))
  refine lt_of_lt_of_le h ((div_le_iff₀' <| mod_cast succ_pos _).mpr ?_)
  rw [right_distrib]
  apply le_add_of_le_of_nonneg
  · exact (div_le_iff₀ hε).mp (le_trans (le_of_lt hN) (mod_cast hi))
  · apply le_of_lt
    simpa

lemma hasSum_mahlerSeries (ha : Tendsto a atTop (�� 0)) :
    HasSum (fun n ↦ mahlerTerm (a n) n) (mahlerSeries a : C(ℤ_[p], E)) := by
  refine (NonarchimedeanAddGroup.summable_of_tendsto_cofinite_zero ?_).hasSum
  rw [tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero] at ha ⊢
  simpa only [norm_mahlerTerm, Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop] using ha

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: Set
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
